title: Delegated onboarding runbook + SLA exemption intake queue
creator: Priya Raman
description: Goal: create a lightweight, repeatable runbook and intake queue pattern for Private/VPC/on-prem customers where network constraints or air-gapped environments require parts of the onboarding work to be delegated to customer operators. The runbook should: 1) standardize the information we ask for up-front (network posture, maintenance windows, proxy/egress allowances, KMS/HSM constraints), 2) define a default exemption SLA pipeline for customers who cannot meet our standard availability or upgrade window requirements, and 3) provide clear templates and automation hooks so Customer Success or Solutions Engineers can progress requests without blocking Engineering for trivial clarifications.
proposal_summary: Introduce a two-track intake: 'Standard Onboarding' (full Redwood-managed path) and 'Delegated Network Onboarding' (customer-managed tasks, with a Redwood validation checklist). Build an 'SLA Exemption Queue' that rates and surfaces exemptions by risk and product impact. Deliverables: runbook doc, intake form template, email templates, an SLA-exemption scoring rubric, a simple dashboard for the queue, automation to generate prefilled issues for ENG/SRE when validation fails.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runbook published in Confluence with step-by-step delegated onboarding checklist and validation steps. 2) Intake form (Zendesk/HubSpot) includes all fields in the checklist and maps to queue tags. 3) Exemption scoring rubric implemented as a spreadsheet + formula and validated with 5 historical customers. 4) Dashboard surfaces outstanding exemptions, average time-to-decision, and number of critical blockers. 5) Two playbook email templates (request for network artifact, escalation to Eng/SRE) exist and have been used at least once by CS in a pilot.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with CS, Solutions Eng, and two customer reps. Agreed scope and two pilot customers (Acme Health, Gravity Payments).

2025-02-18: Drafted delegated onboarding checklist (network-egress, CA pinning, proxy config, IP allowlist windows). Uploaded to draft Confluence at https://confluence.redwood.ai/private/onboarding/delegated-runbook-draft
2025-02-25: Scoring rubric prototypes evaluated against 7 closed tickets; initial thresholds too permissive for maintenance windows — increased risk multiplier for >48h scheduled downtime.

2025-03-01: Implemented intake form skeleton in HubSpot; mapping to ticket tags and CS playbooks agreed. Created GitHub automation idea: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/onboarding-delegated.md to prefill ENG issues when validation fails.

2025-03-05: Pilot 1 (Acme Health) completed delegated checklist remotely; one exemption approved for monthly maintenance window retention. Feedback: need clearer templated network diagrams and a list of required firewall rules per model type.
decision_log: 2025-02-14: Decision to bifurcate intake into Standard vs Delegated tracks to reduce churn in Eng triage queue.
2025-02-24: Decision to use a scoring rubric with three signals (Network Maturity Score, Business Impact Factor, Upgrade Risk Multiplier) rather than free-text risk descriptions.
2025-03-03: Decision to allow limited SLA exemptions (up to 30 days for maintenance windows) with mandatory compensating controls (read-only KV snapshots, extended telemetry window).
2025-03-05: Decision to require all Delegated track customers to provide network diagrams in the specified template before engineer intervention.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers misconfigure and cause production incidents after we delegate network tasks. Mitigation: mandate validation step where Redwood runs smoke tests and KV cache integrity checks post-configuration.

Risk: SLA exemptions become a backdoor to long-term unsupported configurations. Mitigation: exemptions are time-boxed and require renewal with additional controls and exec-level signoff for renewals >90 days.

Risk: Increased operational load on CS and Solutions Eng. Mitigation: create templated artifacts and automation to reduce manual steps; train two CS champions and one Solutions Eng to be the triage owners.
Risk: Security and compliance concerns for air-gapped customers. Mitigation: require security attestation and optional offline installer checks; coordinate with Security for annual review.

pilot_findings: Acme Health: Delegation went smoothly when Templates were used; missing firewall rule examples increased time-to-validate by 2 business days.
Gravity Payments: Needed special handling for HSM/KMS provisioning; required Legal review and a one-week delay to validate offline signer flow.
Both pilots indicated customers prefer a short 'what we will do vs what you must do' matrix at the top of the runbook. Adding that cut back back-and-forth communication.
CS reported the intake form reduces rework by ~35% versus free-form emails in the pilot sample (n=5).
notes_for_engineering: Provide a minimal smoke test harness that validates: connectivity to model storage endpoints, allowed egress destinations, TLS handshake to KMS endpoints, and KV cache sanity. Output should be a pass/fail JSON for automated ingestion.
Expose a small 'validation endpoint' for private installs where customers can upload test results; the intake automation will parse results and assign risk tags.
Consider a 'dry-run' flag in Dedicated that executes the smoke tests without changing runtime state to speed validation for delegated onboardings.
Add flagging to the rollout system to prevent automatic upgrades for customers with active exemptions and add an opt-in manual upgrade flow handled by Solutions Eng.
